# Context-Rich Solid Mechanics Problem

## Torsional Stiffness of a Variable-Radius Aluminum Drive Shaft

### Engineering Context

A mechanical engineering team is evaluating a lightweight aluminum torque-transmission shaft for a precision industrial drive or torsion-test system. The shaft radius increases continuously from the torque-input end toward a rigid mounting interface. This geometry reduces material near the small end while providing much greater torsional stiffness near the support.

Excessive input-end rotation can create positioning error, misalignment, or poor control response. The shaft is modeled as a solid circular member made from 2014-T6 aluminum alloy with constant shear modulus and a prescribed radius profile.

![Variable-radius aluminum shaft installed in an industrial drivetrain or torsion-test assembly.](assets/tapered-shaft-industry-context.png){fig-alt="Long tapered metallic shaft connected between industrial drive and support equipment." width=88%}

### Main Engineering Goal

Determine the angular rotation of end A relative to the fixed mounting interface, locate the maximum torsional shear stress, identify the region dominating compliance, and assess the shaft against its twist limit.

### System Components

- variable-radius solid 2014-T6 aluminum shaft;
- torque-input coupling at end A;
- rigid fixed mounting interface at the large end;
- connected drive or test equipment.
